citations.narrative:
The registrant has not kept or maintained copies of every health certificate for dogs or cats that her facility has transported
in commerce.
The registrant is primarily a dog ground transporter. The registrant stated that she requires health certificates and reviews
them for compliance but does not keep a copy of the every health certificate. A portion of the health certificates required
to be kept by this section were available for review during the inspection. The registrant stated she was unaware of the
requirements of this section.
APHIS officials review health certificates to track animal movements and verify the transporter's compliance with § 2.78.
In connection with all live dogs or cats delivered for transportation in commerce, the accepting carrier shall keep and
maintain a copy of the health certification completed as required by § 2.78, tendered with each live dog or cat.
Correction date: 8/7/2026.

citations.desc: Primary enclosures used to transport live dogs and cats.
citations.narrative:
The transport enclosures used by the registrant do not have the “Live Animals” and arrow labeling.
Proper labeling of a transport enclosure is important for the safety of the animals during transportation and to provide
handling guidance to transport personnel.
Since the enclosures are not permanently affixed to the transport conveyance (truck/van, etc), the words “Live Animals”
must be marked on top and on one or more sides in letters at least 1 inch (2.5cm) high, and with arrows or other markings
to indicate the correct upright position of the primary enclosure.
Correct by the next animal transport.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the registrant.

Proper labeling of a transport enclosure is important for the safety of the animals during transportation and to provide
